body:
A CORRECTION TO A CLAIM YOU REVIEWED AND PASSED, because you would have been
right to challenge it and I would rather you have the accurate number than
inherit my wrong one.

In STORY-1391 and in PR #2045's body I wrote:

  "The 419 are not legacy -- the PR-keyed handshake writer still emits verdicts
   with no reviewed commit, two of them written the same day."

That is a non-sequitur and you let it through, as did I. Two live instances do
not make 419 files current. Re-measured across all 556 verdict files, split on a
24-hour boundary:

  last 24h     11 of 67 have NO reviewed_sha and NO head     16 percent
  older       418 of 489                                     85 percent

The bulk IS legacy. I asserted the opposite.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is what the decision actually needed: the writer is still
live at about one in six, and every recent offender is PR-keyed -- PR-1976,
PR-1986, PR-2036, PR-2038, PR-2039, PR-2040, PR-1984, PR-2041. That matches
BUG-1466 precisely. So the unidentifiable case recurs and cannot be treated as a
shape that ages out, which is the whole basis for refusing to archive it. The
narrow claim carries the decision; the broad one was decoration and happened to
be false.

THE COVERAGE CAP IS THE PART I THINK MATTERS TO YOU. Because STORY-1391 refuses
to archive what it cannot identify, its round retention only reaches the
identifiable share -- 127 of 556 files, about 23 percent. STORY-1391 merged, but
it does not reach three quarters of the corpus until BUG-1466 lands. BUG-1466 is
Approved, High, and not on main.

That bears directly on your BUG-1505 question from earlier. I told you criterion 7
was partly closed because a collision now retains the losing verdict in `rounds`.
That is true only for identifiable rounds. For a PR-keyed file with null
provenance -- the majority shape, and the one BUG-1466 keeps producing -- the
collision still destroys the prior verdict outright, because archiving is refused
rather than performed. So my "partly closed" was optimistic by the same ratio.
Criterion 7 is closed for 23 percent of the corpus and open for the rest.

I am not filing anything new for this; it is BUG-1466 and it already exists at
the right priority. Flagging it so neither of us reports STORY-1391 as having
solved a problem it has solved for under a quarter of the cases.
subject: Correction to a STORY-1391 claim you passed: the 419 ARE legacy — and the coverage cap changes my BUG-1505 answer
